ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a large square; the top row is divided by vertical lines into four congruent small squares; this top row exactly spans the entire width of the large square. Below the top small squares is a single rectangle, which also spans the entire width of the large square, and together with the four top small squares forms the entire large square. Reasoning: Let the side length of each small square be s. Since the four small squares are arranged in a row and fill the top side of the large square, the side length of the large square is 4s. The horizontal length of the rectangle below is equal to the side length of the large square, therefore it is 4s. The vertical width of the rectangle equals the total height of the large square minus the height of the top small squares, namely 4s - s = 3s. Therefore, the length of the rectangle is (4s)/(3s) = 4/3 times its width.

Let each small square have side length s. Since four small squares exactly fill the top edge, the side length of the large square is 4s. The rectangle below has the same horizontal length as the large square, so its length is 4s. Its vertical width is the large square height minus the top-row square height: 4s - s = 3s. Therefore the rectangle's length is (4s)/(3s) = 4/3 times its width.
